New machine. Its objects are: lupuze, dosikas, vuvepo, zokapun, zavafan, ziludak.
You have 4 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: lupuze, dosikas, vuvepo
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The first three gave no light, but I don't yet know the machine's rule. It might light when any nexiom is present, or only when both are. Testing the other three objects will help separate those cases.

TEST: zokapun, zavafan, ziludak
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Both rule ideas agree on where the nexioms are. If any single nexiom lights the machine, none are in the first group, so both are in the second. If both are needed, the second group must contain both. Either way, the pair is among zokapun, zavafan and ziludak, giving three possible pairs.

I still don't know which rule the machine uses, so I'll test one object on its own.
- If ziludak alone lights it up, a single nexiom is enough and ziludak is one of them.
- If it doesn't light up, either the machine needs both nexioms, or the pair is zokapun and zavafan.

With only two tests and the rule unknown, I may not be able to separate every case.

TEST: ziludak
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Ziludak alone did not light the machine. Here is what each rule allows:
- **If any single nexiom lights the machine:** ziludak is not a nexiom, so the pair is zokapun and zavafan.
- **If the machine needs both nexioms:** ziludak alone could never light it, so any of the three pairs is still possible: zokapun+zavafan, zokapun+ziludak or zavafan+ziludak.

No single test can separate all three pairs, so I'll test the pair that fits both rules.
- If zokapun and zavafan together light up, they are the nexioms under either rule.
- If they don't, the machine needs both nexioms and the pair includes ziludak. I would then have to guess between zokapun+ziludak and zavafan+ziludak.

TEST: zokapun, zavafan
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Zokapun and zavafan together did not light the machine, so the "any single nexiom" rule is ruled out. Under that rule they would have to be the nexioms and would have lit it. The machine must need both nexioms present, which means the pair includes ziludak.

That leaves zokapun+ziludak or zavafan+ziludak. My tests cannot tell these apart, so this answer is a 50/50 guess.

ANSWER: nexioms = zokapun, ziludak
One last question. If only ziludak were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No. I tested ziludak on its own in my third test and the machine did not light up. Its response is fixed, so the same setup should give the same result. This is also consistent with my conclusion that the machine needs both nexioms present at once: even if ziludak is a nexiom, as I believe, it can't light the machine alone.

PROBE: no

Checking every pair against all three tests leaves 4 candidates:
- dovorek + forivak
- dovorek + zezefok
- forivak + zezefok
- forivak + nevevan

One yes/no test can at best split these 2 and 2. I'll test forivak, zezefok and nevevan:
- **If it lights:** the pair is forivak+zezefok or forivak+nevevan.
- **If it doesn't light:** the pair is dovorek+forivak or dovorek+zezefok.

Either way my final answer will be a 50/50 choice between the two left.

TEST: forivak, zezefok, nevevan
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Test 4 (forivak, zezefok, nevevan) lit, so under the both-needed rule the pair is forivak + zezefok or forivak + nevevan. Forivak is a nexiom either way. Nothing I've seen separates zezefok from nevevan, so this is a 50/50 guess on the second one, and I'm choosing zezefok.

ANSWER: nexioms = forivak, zezefok
One last question. If only forivak were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

**No.** Forivak alone would not light the machine.

- **Test 3** (dovorek, nevevan, lofove) did not light. If any single nexiom were enough, that would rule out dovorek, nevevan and lofove. **Test 1** (zezefok, nevevan, goduza) would rule out zezefok and goduza. That leaves only forivak, but there are two nexioms, so the "any nexiom" rule is impossible.
- **Under the both-needed rule**, which my answer relied on, forivak is a nexiom but needs its partner, so alone it does nothing.
- **There is one other rule I didn't consider earlier:** the machine lights only when exactly one nexiom is present. That also fits all four results, with zezefok and goduza as the pair. Under it, forivak is not a nexiom, so alone it would still not light.

So I'm fairly confident in "no," though less sure of my earlier answer than I made it sound.
